$comment: Gzip ceilings (bytes) for the BUILT site, checked by scripts/check-site-perf-budget.ts in deploy-site.yml after a real `jx build`. A page ceiling covers the HTML plus every same-origin asset that HTML eagerly references, derived from the built markup rather than listed here. Raise a ceiling deliberately, with justification, when a real feature grows it.
$baseline: Measured on the build that minified browser bundles, inlined component CSS, emitted modulepreload hints, stopped emitting the search corpus twice, and made the search client a lazy import. Before that change the same home page cost 50,651 gz bytes across 18 requests and every visitor also downloaded search-index.json (409,178 gz) whether or not they searched — 491 KiB total, which is what prompted these budgets.
$ratchet-search-index: Change review's documentation (studio/publish/source-control.md gains a 'Read a change' section, plus a Diff section in interface/modes.md and one in logic/code.md) moved the index 392824 -> 394495 gz bytes, +1671. The 375000 ceiling was already being met on TOLERANCE rather than under the ceiling: main sat at 104.8%, with 926 bytes of the 5% allowance left, so this was the growth that happened to cross rather than the growth that was unusual. Raised to just above the measured figure so the index is under its CEILING again and the tolerance is headroom for noise rather than the thing holding it up. The index is a pure function of the docs corpus, and this repository requires a behaviour change to ship its documentation in the same change set, so it grows whenever the docs do; the lever if it needs shrinking is the corpus the search client actually needs, not the prose.
$ratchet-search-index-spec-pages: The three reference pages derived from the specs left the index (#305): the spec changelog, implementation status and the standards table now carry search: false in their frontmatter, which @jxsuite/search's emit honours per entry. Removed: the spec changelog (20 documents, 6.4% of the raw index), the standards table (10, 2.5%) and implementation status (7, 0.3%): 37 of 1,449 documents, and the index moved 445035 -> 399469 gz bytes, -45566 (-10.2%). The generated CATALOGUES stay in — formulas, operators, commands, shortcuts, starters, routes, 4.2% together — because a formula name or a keyboard shortcut should land on the page that lists it, so the lever took what a reader never searches for and left what a reader does. The 445000 ceiling was the kit-docs ratchet, raised from 395000 when docs/extending/ui-kit.md, the embedding pages and ~40 spec releases' changelog entries arrived together (+48861); that note named this opt-out as the lever, and it recovered most of the raise. Lowered to just above the measured figure, on this file's own rule: the index is a pure function of the corpus the search client actually needs, and a hand-written page is real documentation, so the kit page stays.
$ratchet-search-index-vault-guide: The vault-as-content change shipped its documentation in the same change set, as this repository requires: a new guide (Obsidian vault as content, 14.4 KB of raw index text) and additions to content collections (+9.4 KB), Jx Markdown (+3.5 KB), routing, search, feeds, relationships, the build pipeline and the Studio content-types page. That moved the index 418634 -> 424692 gz bytes on the CI build, +6058, which crossed the +5% tolerance over the 401000 ceiling (the ceiling was already being met on tolerance, at 104.4% on main). Raised to just above the measured figure so the index is under its CEILING again. The review of that change then asked for more documentation (an Upgrading section, what an excluded file's asset mount refuses, symlinks, attachments, callout types, where against filter), which took the index to 427331 gz bytes, +2639 over the first figure, so the ceiling is 428000 for the same reason. The same change also made pages with code samples SMALLER in the index (-2.4 KB raw across ~30 pages): a sample containing a template-looking `${` used to be evaluated into the binding's value, so the index held 'undefined' where the code was, and it now holds the code. No page was opted out and nothing the search client needs was removed; the lever, as the entries above say, is the corpus the client actually needs, not the prose.
